distractors.reason: We don't say 'big letter' for an upper-case letter. 'Big' describes size in general, not the case of a letter.
'Large' describes physical size. We don't use it to name upper-case letters.
'Tall' describes height, so 'tall letter' does not refer to upper-case letters.

example_sentence: Your name starts with a ___ letter.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes pueden decir 'big letter' porque 'grande' se usa para casi todo, pero en inglés la mayúscula se llama 'capital letter'.
explanation: In English, 'capital' is the standard adjective for upper-case letters. Think of it as the 'top' or 'main' form of a letter, which is why it is used with 'letter' rather than words about size.

related_collocations.example: London is the capital city of England.
The child kicked the red ball across the yard.
There is a tall tree in the garden.

memory_tip: CAPITAL = the top or main form (capital letter, capital city) | BIG / LARGE / TALL = size or height, not letter case
